dc's record read of hv's todo 40, for your synthesis to hv: read only, nothing changed (2026-11-19 05:10Z by date -u).

STANDS? As an open item, yes. devbin still declares no "formatters" key, so Intent's staged-format guard answers not applicable: it is the one "skipped" on devbin's commit gate line. The item's premise is wrong, though: check format does not cover Markdown at run time either. It checks declared languages only, and here it prints "no formattable language declared" (lib/cmd/check:283). Markdown is out of the gate on purpose: ST0001's AC-15.6 (issue 0003, asserted by AT-15.13) keeps it out because prettier re-pads the tables this repo hand-aligns. Measured today with prettier 3.10.1 --list-different, which writes nothing: 93 of 332 tracked .md files would change. 74 are frozen .history/ archives. The rest include README.md (table padding), docs/authoring-commands.md (emphasis markers), four bin/.devbin/help pages, and CHANGELOG.md and RELEASES.md, which are generated views that release check regenerates and compares, so no hand reformat can hold. All 35 vendored lib/ pages are prettier-stable, held by tests/unit/vendoredmd.bats.

QUESTION: Should devbin declare "formatters": ["markdown"], so its commit gate refuses staged Markdown that prettier would rewrite?

FOR: it closes hv's todo 40, open since 2026-09-22, and settles whether devbin's Markdown answers to prettier at commit time or stays hand-laid with no gate.

(a) No. Markdown stays ungated, as AC-15.6 already rules for the run gate, and todo 40 closes on the corrected record. Nothing in the tree changes.
(b) Yes, whole. Declare it, reformat the live files (which re-lays the hand-aligned tables), change lib/release.notes to emit prettier's layout (shipped code, so every consumer's generated views change too), and reverse AC-15.6's exclusion and its test. If the declaration lands before the generator changes, the next release-note commit is refused.
(c) Yes, narrowly. Declare it and list every non-stable file in .prettierignore, so only files already stable are checked. That is a hand-kept second list of which files are hand-laid, for a check vendoredmd.bats already makes on the files consumers receive.

RECOMMENDATION: (a). The gap is deliberate, and the one surface where prettier-stability matters, the pages a consumer's own guard will check, is already held. (b) gives up a ruled design and changes shipped code for a style devbin chose not to have; (c) adds a list that drifts.

For vc, not hv (off-path, no work): bare `bin/devbin fmt md` sweeps ./*.md, so here it would re-pad README.md's tables and rewrite the two generated views, which by .prettierignore's own rule (a generated view has one writer, its renderer) no formatter should touch. And a consumer that declares markdown and generates the same views would have its note commit refused (unmeasured).
